title: On‑Prem POC: Quant & Model Decision Log for Sensitive Data Assistant
body:
TL;DR: This doc captures the decision process and experiment log for a customer POC that requires on‑prem inference (air‑gapped option) with sensitive data. Goal is to pick a model + quantization profile that balances hallucination risk, p95 latency, and memory footprint for a single‑rack deployment (2x A10G or 1x A100 equivalent). We recommend running a 13B model in 4-bit GPTQ (q4_k_m / NF4 variant) as the baseline for the initial canary, with a 7B q4_0 fallback for high‑latency events. Keep all KV/prefix caching enabled in Redwood with small (128–256 token) warm caches for frequent prompts.

Context and constraints
- Customer: large regulated enterprise (finance/insurance) running PII-heavy support assistant.
- Deployment: Private (VPC / on‑prem) with restricted egress, KMS integration required for keys. No upstream telemetry allowed; metrics exported only to customer prometheus endpoint.
- HW available for POC: options 2x A10G (24GB ea) or single A100-40GB. Memory budget per model process must stay under ~36GB to allow space for OS and Redwood runtime.
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 350 ms for short responses (<= 80 tokens). Prefer p95 < 200 ms if possible for snappier UX. Token cost is secondary but still tracked.

POC objectives
1) Functional parity vs the hosted baseline: answers should be >= baseline fidelity on 50 curated eval prompts (scored by SMEs).
2) Latency/throughput profile that meets customer SLOs on the available HW.
3) Memory fit for private deployment without multi‑node model sharding (single GPU process preferred).
4) A clear fallback/rollout plan using Redwood routing (model variant + capacity tiers).

Model candidates considered (shortlist)
- OpenModel‑7B (7B dense / instruction‑tuned) — pros: small, cheap; cons: weaker factuality vs 13B
- OpenModel‑13B (13B instruction tuned) — sweet spot for quality vs resource needs
- OpenModel‑30B (30B) — higher quality but fails single GPU constraint without sharding
- Falcon‑Instruct‑Large (7B/40B variants considered) — good instruction tuning but larger memory
- Local quantized Llama2 variants (13B / 70B in theory) — 70B impossible on single GPU budget

Quantization approaches evaluated
- 8‑bit PTQ (int8 / awq): fast to generate, lower accuracy drop, larger memory than 4‑bit.
- 4‑bit GPTQ (q4_0, q4_k_m, nf4): best memory footprint; some quality regressions on numeric reasoning but acceptable on instruction tasks.
- 3‑bit experimental: only evaluated as research; not used for POC.

Experiment matrix (summary)
- Test harness: 50 prompt eval set (mix of short support queries, multi‑turn clarifications, and safety boundary cases). Throughput/latency measured using Redwood bench harness with 1 thread per request, and a separate batched load test.
- Hardware: A10G x2 (used as single GPU for these runs). OS + runtime overhead ~4.5GB.

Key runs and results (representative)
1) OpenModel‑13B, float16
- Memory: ~38GB (OOM on single A10G) -> ruled out for single‑GPU float16.
- Qualitative: best answers, but not viable for single GPU.

2) OpenModel‑13B, q4_k_m (GPTQ, NF4 style)
- Memory: ~17–19GB on A10G
- Latency (p95, single request, gen up to 80 tokens): 220–280 ms
- Throughput: ~20–25 tokens/sec
- Accuracy vs eval: 92/100 (SME scoring)
- Notes: small regressions on numeric precision prompts; prompt rephrasing reduced failures.

3) OpenModel‑13B, q4_0 (lighter GPTQ)
- Memory: ~15–17GB
- Latency p95: 190–240 ms
- Throughput: ~24–30 tokens/sec
- Accuracy: 88/100
- Notes: slightly faster but lower fidelity on edgecases.

4) OpenModel‑7B, q4_0
- Memory: ~8–9GB
- Latency p95: 110–150 ms
- Throughput: ~40–55 tokens/sec
- Accuracy: 80/100
- Notes: Good fallback for latency/cost but more hallucinations on rare requests.

5) Falcon‑instruct‑7B, q4_k_m
- Memory ~16 GB
- Latency p95 ~200–260 ms
- Accuracy 86/100
- Notes: similar to 13B q4_0 in some prompt families but inconsistent on policy questions.

Decision and recommendation
- Baseline model for canary: OpenModel‑13B in q4_k_m (balance of fidelity and memory). Rationale: fits single GPU, high SME score, p95 close to SLO and can be reduced further with prompt/pipeline changes.
- Fallback route: OpenModel‑7B q4_0 for degraded mode (latency spike or heavy traffic). This is small and can be spun up quickly.
- Avoid 30B for single‑node POC; consider multi‑GPU sharding only for later stages.

Prompt & pipeline tuning (to reduce latency and improve quality)
- System prompt compression: move boilerplate from per‑request system to server‑side per‑session metadata where possible. Use placeholders in runtime and expand only when needed.
- Template minimalism: remove long examples from top of prompts; move few representative examples into a cached context that is attached once per session (prefix cache).
- Instruction normalization: canonicalize user input (shorten long trailing context) before sending to model; detect structured inputs and call function hooks if appropriate.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable auto prefix caching for repeated tasks (support ticket templates). Cache size: 128–256 tokens empirically hit best tradeoff.
- Early stop & streaming: prefer streaming token output to UI and auto‑stop generation when answer completes (detect end tokens / heuristics) to save tokens and reduce perceived latency.

Redwood runtime config knobs to use
- Enable continuous batching with max latency window 15ms for background interactions; disable for ultra‑low latency endpoints.
- Configure model routing policy: primary=13B_q4_k_m, fallback=7B_q4_0; capacity tiers: reserve 1 instance per customer for low burst allowance.
- KV cache retention: 30s default + session affinity for 95th percentile repeated queries.

Rollout plan
1) Internal QA: run 2,000 synthetic conversations (nightly) comparing 13B_q4_k_m vs hosted baseline; track hallucination/regression metrics (automated eval harness).
2) Canary (customer): 5% traffic for 48 hours, watch p95 latency, user satisfaction proxies, and failed safety checks. If hallucination delta > 3% vs baseline, pause.
3) Gradual ramp: 5 -> 25 -> 50% with automated rollback on latency/SLA breaches.

Metrics to capture in POC
- p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, 95th percentile memory usage.
- SME scoring on random sample (daily 50 prompts).
- Hallucination rate (QA checked) and safety flags.
- Cost proxy (tokens * model cost factor) and instance hours.

Experiment log (selected entries)
- 2024‑03‑15: Initial 13B float16 test failed (OOM) — confirmed need for 4‑bit.
- 2024‑03‑18: GPTQ q4_k_m produced best SME score; initial latency p95 280ms.
- 2024‑03‑22: Prompt compression + KV caching reduced p95 to ~220ms (single GPU).
- 2024‑03‑26: Implemented fallback routing in Redwood console; smoke tests pass.
- 2024‑03‑30: Canary dry run with synthetic traffic — scaled to 5% with no regression in SME metrics.

Open questions / risks
- KMS/HSM integration latency: snapshot shows key unwrap adds ~8–12 ms per session; need to bench at scale.
- Numeric reasoning degradation in q4_k_m: can we add post‑processing checks/validators for numbers? (JIRA-POC-1423)
- Regulatory audit: need to produce deterministic logs for a subset of requests; check that quantized model determinism aligns with requirements.

Next actions (owner: Avery Chen)
- [ ] Finalize canary runbook & rollback criteria (due 2024‑04‑05)
- [ ] Add automated numeric validators to pipeline (Priya to prototype)
- [ ] Confirm HSM latency with infra (Marcus)
- [ ] Prepare customer facing one‑pager with expected SLOs and fallbacks

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working doc: expect shorthand and links to tickets. If you see missing eval families we should add them (legal/policy Qs, long‑form summarization, multi‑turn escalation flow). Feedback especially welcome on fallback thresholds and cache sizing recommendations.
